entry.title: torquoselectivity
entry.content:
By the Woodward-Hoffmann rules, a \(4\pi\) ring opening is conrotatory. However, for some asymmetrically substituted cyclobutenes, there is another type of selectivity that depends on which way the ring opens, called torquoselectivity. I originally thought this just progressed through sterics, i.e., the bulky group would rotate outwards, but it turns out that in 1984, the Houk group found some \(4\pi\) openings that do not do this. For example:

The left-hand product (Z) is favored despite the (E) product being thermodynamically favorable.

So what favors inward rotation?

As we can see, the HOMO has \(\sigma\) character, and the LUMO has \(\sigma^*\) character and can interact with substituents’ p-orbitals.

The figure shows the frontier orbitals in the transition state, with possible substituent locations.

What happens if the substituent rotates inward?

As we can see, the substituent will stabilize the HOMO and destabilize the LUMO. Thus, electron-donating substituents will tend to rotate outwards because of the destabilizing interaction with the LUMO. Conversely, acceptor substituents will rotate inwards due to the stabilizing interaction with the HOMO. (The LUMOs are empty, so there is no destabilizing interaction).

Sources: https://chemistry.stackexchange.com/questions/81188/stereoelectronic-effects-in-torquoselectivity-of-4%CF%80-electrocyclic-opening

Rondan, N. G.; Houk, K. N. Theory of stereoselection in conrotatory electrocyclic reactions of substituted cyclobutenes. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1985, 107 (7), 2099–2111. DOI: 10.1021/ja00293a046
